title: Three BSF Personnel and Several Villagers Injured in Clash at Tripura's Ashabari
excerpt: Villagers allege a local youth was detained and beaten, fracturing his leg, sparking a road blockade that turned violent. The chief minister condemned the assault on BSF personnel and ordered strict action; both sides have filed complaints.
body:
• Three Border Security Force personnel and several local residents were injured in a clash at Ashabari, Tripura, on Monday, November 2.
  • Local residents allege the clash began after BSF personnel detained a youth, Hefzur Rahman, around 10 a.m. and assaulted him, fracturing his leg.
  • Protesters blocked the Ashabari-Rahimpur road and allegedly attacked a 49th Battalion vehicle carrying Company Commander Rohit, driver Sunil Kumar and jawan Manjit with sticks and bamboo.
  • Tripura Chief Minister Manik Saha condemned the assault on BSF personnel and directed swift, stringent action; complaints have been lodged by both sides and an inquiry is under way.

Three Border Security Force (BSF) personnel and several local residents were injured in a clash at Ashabari in Tripura's Sepahijala district on Monday, following an alleged assault on a local youth by BSF personnel, according to InsightNE News. Tension continued to prevail in the area, which falls under Kalamchaura police station in the Sonamura sub-division, near the Bangladesh border.

What residents say happened

According to local residents, the incident began around 10 a.m. when BSF personnel allegedly detained Hefzur Rahman, son of Shahajan Mia, on suspicion while he was working near New Bazar Road, adjacent to the Ashabari Gram Panchayat. Locals alleged he was assaulted during detention, resulting in a fractured leg.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2117315623172948460

Angry residents then blocked the Ashabari-Rahimpur road near New Bazar and staged a protest demanding action over the alleged assault, with many women joining the blockade. The situation escalated when a vehicle carrying three personnel of the 49th BSF Battalion — Company Commander Rohit, driver Sunil Kumar and jawan Manjit — passed through the area from Rahimpur towards Boxanagar. The vehicle was reportedly surrounded by protesters, who allegedly attacked the personnel with sticks and bamboo, leaving all three injured.

The official response

Tripura Chief Minister Manik Saha condemned the assault on the BSF personnel and directed the authorities to take swift and stringent action. "I strongly condemn the brutal assault on our brave BSF personnel at Ashabari by a group of miscreants. Such acts of violence against our security forces are completely unacceptable," he said, in remarks reported by NDTV from a syndicated feed. That report described the attackers as alleged smugglers and said they reportedly attempted to snatch firearms from the injured personnel and vandalised a government vehicle.

The two accounts frame the clash differently — residents describe a protest over a detained youth; the syndicated report describes an attack by alleged smugglers — and the circumstances are yet to be established through investigation, InsightNE News reported.

Injuries, complaints and inquiry

The injured BSF personnel were initially taken to Boxanagar Hospital and later referred to hospital care in Agartala. Personnel from the Ashabari BSF border outpost and Kalamchaura police reached the spot and brought the situation under control. Complaints have been lodged by both sides at the police station, and senior BSF officials visited the area and initiated an inquiry into the incident.
